title: pvVisItM3DReader
body:
## pvVisItM3DReader

Reads output of M3D, the multilevel 3-D MHD code for fusion plasmas (.m3d, .h5): an unstructured mesh named "mesh" with node-centred fields over the stored time steps. ParaView 5.13.3 has no native M3D reader; for M3D-C1 output use pvVisItM3DC1Reader. One file supplies every time step the format stores.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- M3D and M3D-C1 are different codes and formats; pick the reader that matches the code that wrote the file.
- Name the arrays you need in PointArrays and CellArrays: the VisIt bridge starts with every variable unselected, so omitting them normally gives geometry without fields.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue and has not run a native acceptance check for this reader; check meshes, arrays and times on your own data.

Native constructor: `VisItM3DReader`. Identity: `sources/VisItM3DReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CellArrays` | Names of the zone-centred (cell) variables to read from M3D data; each becomes a cell-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. The M3D plugin declares its variables node-centred, so this list normally stays empty. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `FileName` | Path of the single M3D file to read (.m3d, .h5); the reader takes every time step the format stores from it. Use an absolute path; relative paths are not resolved against the JSON file's folder (Studio uses the directory it was launched from). Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Materials` | Names of materials to convert into volume-fraction cell arrays. For each selected material the bridge adds a float cell array named after it: 1 in cells made only of that material, its volume fraction in mixed cells and -1 where it is absent. The M3D plugin defines no materials, so this list has nothing to select. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Meshes` | Names of the M3D meshes to read. Each selected mesh becomes one named block of the multiblock output and unlisted meshes are skipped. The M3D plugin reports one unstructured mesh named "mesh". | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `PointArrays` | Names of the node-centred (point) variables to read from M3D data; each becomes a point-data array on every selected mesh that defines it. Vector variables arrive as one multi-component array, while VisIt expressions and tensor, label, species and array variables are not converted by the bridge. For M3D data these are the node-centred fields of the M3D output. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvVisItM3DReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
